result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers open with a clear no and reject the claim that the script makes a site compliant or protects it from lawsuits, and both suggest testing the key flows by keyboard and screen reader and speaking to a lawyer. B is slightly fairer about the toolbar, calling it harmless as an extra courtesy feature. It also raises the risk of putting a third-party script on checkout pages and lists fixes specific to a shop, such as variant selectors. A is dismissive of the toolbar's value, but it does point out more directly that most fixes are made once per template, not separately on each of the sixty pages. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give a clear 'don't buy it as the fix' verdict and explain well why overlays can't deliver compliance or legal protection. B fits the sixty-page shop better: it says most fixes happen at the template level rather than as sixty separate jobs, and it recommends seeing a lawyer about legal assurance in any case. A is somewhat fairer about the toolbar's value, calling it harmless as an extra, and it raises the third-party script risk. Even so, B's template focus and its questions for the sales rep make it slightly more practical.
